tariffs.tariff_name: Data Center Power Service / Mobile Data Center tariffs
tariffs.status_detail: PUCO adopted the settlement July 9, 2025; compliance tariff effective July 23, 2025.
tariffs.summary: First-in-the-nation, data-center-specific tariff requiring new large data centers to pay for at least 85% of their contracted capacity for up to 12 years, even if they use less, to insulate other ratepayers from stranded-investment risk.

min_load.detail: Applies to data centers of 25 MW and larger (and mobile data centers ≥1 MW).

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Customers billed on a minimum monthly demand floor regardless of usage.

customer_type.detail: Scoped to data centers / mobile data centers; excludes electrified manufacturing.

credit_collateral.detail: Requires A-/A3 credit rating or collateral equal to 50% of total minimum charges.

contracted_capacity.detail: 85% minimum demand charge; service may be suspended if usage exceeds contract capacity by >1 MW.

resize_reassign.detail: Customers may assign up to 25% of contracted capacity to another customer when exiting.

contract_duration.detail: Up to 12-year commitment to the minimum-demand obligation.

ramp_times.detail: Up to a 4-year load ramp: ≥50% yr1, 65% yr2, 80% yr3, 90% yr4 of contract capacity.

exit_fee.detail: Exit fee equal to 3 years of minimum charges.

additional_terms.detail: PUCO ordered AEP Ohio to immediately lift its moratorium on connecting new data centers.

legislation.title: Ohio House Bill 15 (2025)
legislation.summary: Restructured Ohio's electricity market (removed Electric Security Plans, enabled behind-the-meter self-power) to attract data centers while protecting ratepayers.

tariffs.source_title: PUCO — Order directing AEP Ohio to create a data-center-specific tariff

resources.title: AEP Ohio — Data Center Tariff page

tariffs.tariff_name: Clean Transition Tariff (CTT)
tariffs.status_detail: Filed 2024; pending before the PUCN as of the LBL brief.
tariffs.summary: Optional tariff letting large industrial customers access new clean-energy resources by paying a premium; Google's 15-year service agreement would recover the cost of an enhanced-geothermal resource powering its data centers.

btm_backup.detail: Customers may install customer-owned or leased back-up generation or storage.

contract_duration.detail: Long-term energy-supply period; Google's service agreement runs 15 years.

clean_energy.detail: Customers pay a premium to access new clean-energy resources matched to their load.

specific_generation.detail: Utility procures a named resource (enhanced geothermal) on the customer's behalf.

marginal_pricing.detail: Premium is designed so incremental clean-resource costs are assigned to the customer, not shared.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — NV Energy Clean Transition Tariff (PUCN 24-05022/23)

tariffs.tariff_name: Callisto Energy Supply Agreement
tariffs.status_detail: Pending before the PUCN as of the LBL brief.
tariffs.summary: A bespoke energy-supply agreement for a large-load customer whose exit terms are tied to the price difference between the procured resource and NV Energy's most recent approved renewable facilities.

exit_fee.detail: Termination payment based on the price difference between the procurement-agreement rate and NV Energy's most recent approved renewable facilities, net of expected generation.

clean_energy.detail: Supply tied to commission-approved renewable facilities.

specific_generation.detail: Procures a specific resource on the customer's behalf.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — NV Energy Callisto ESA (PUCN 24-06014)

tariffs.utility: Indiana Michigan Power (I&M, an AEP utility)
tariffs.tariff_name: Tariff I.P. — Industrial Power (large-load settlement)
tariffs.status_detail: IURC approved the settlement Feb 2025 (filed Nov 2024).
tariffs.summary: A 'landmark' settlement among I&M, the state consumer counselor, Citizens Action Coalition, Amazon, Google, Microsoft and the Data Center Coalition setting minimum-take, collateral and exit terms for large loads, plus low-income community payments.

min_load.detail: 70 MW minimum at an individual plant, or 150 MW on an aggregated basis.

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Monthly demand charge no less than the greater of 80% of contract capacity or 80% of the highest billing demand in the prior 11 months; plus a minimum monthly charge.

study_cost_recovery.detail: Customers must pay for full planning studies, including steady-state and dynamic studies.

credit_collateral.detail: Collateral satisfied via parent/affiliate guarantee (min rating + liquidity), an A-/A3 letter of credit, or cash.

resize_reassign.detail: Contract capacity may be reduced up to 20% after the first 5 years, with ≥42 months' notice before the PJM delivery year.

contract_duration.detail: 12-year minimum initial contract term after the load-ramp period ends.

exit_fee.detail: Exit fee equal to the remaining minimum-bill charge for terminated/reduced capacity above the allowed 20% reduction.

econ_dev_payments.detail: Amazon, Google and Microsoft each provide $500,000/year for 5 years to the Indiana Community Action Association for weatherization of income-qualified customers.

tariffs.source_title: AEP — Indiana Michigan Power receives order in large-load settlement

resources.title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025)

tariffs.tariff_name: Electric Service Agreement with Blocke, LLC (Meta)
tariffs.summary: A special service agreement for a Meta subsidiary that uses a dedicated power-purchase agreement kept out of the utility's integrated resource plan, so the data center's supply does not affect other customers.

marginal_pricing.detail: Dedicated PPA is excluded from the IRP and does not affect other customers; the customer pays its transmission share via the open-access transmission tariff.

specific_generation.detail: Supply backed by a dedicated power-purchase agreement for the customer.

contracted_capacity.detail: Customer pays its load-ratio share of associated transmission upgrades.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — Duke Energy Indiana / Meta ESA (IURC 45975)

tariffs.tariff_name: Competitive Response Rider / Google Electric Service Agreement
tariffs.summary: A negotiated, discounted large-load rider for customers that could otherwise obtain third-party supply, with a hold-harmless test ensuring incremental costs to serve the customer are offset by incremental revenue.

min_load.detail: 2 MW for existing customers; 10 MW for new customers, with the ability to grow to 75 MW within 5 years.

resize_reassign.detail: Negotiated discount may not exceed the gap between the standard tariff and the customer's lowest-cost competitive supply.

duration_flexibility.detail: Customers may renew for an additional 10 years if they maintain ≥75 MW firm peak demand during their final 2 years.

exit_fee.detail: 1-year termination notice plus a payment equal to the net book value of incremental facilities built to serve the data center.

marginal_pricing.detail: Energy services agreement passes a 'regulatory incremental cost test' so incremental costs are offset by incremental revenues (hold-harmless).

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — Xcel Minnesota Competitive Response Rider (MPUC 19-39)

tariffs.tariff_name: Brisbie Energy Services Agreement / Clean Energy Your Way
tariffs.summary: An energy-services agreement in which Idaho Power procures renewable resources on a data center's behalf and connects them to its transmission system; the customer pays for the resources and its load-ratio share of the grid, and is credited for system value.

contracted_capacity.detail: Customer pays its load-ratio share of Idaho Power's generation and transmission used to back its load.

clean_energy.detail: Schedule 19 customers may buy RECs, subscribe to a shared new renewable resource, or build a dedicated renewable resource (Clean Energy Your Way).

specific_generation.detail: Utility procures renewable resources on the customer's behalf and interconnects them directly to its transmission system.

marginal_pricing.detail: Customer is credited for the value its renewables bring to the system, a cost/benefit alignment (hold-harmless).

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — Idaho Power Brisbie ESA (IPUC IPC-E-21-42)

tariffs.tariff_name: High Density Contracted Demand Response Rate
tariffs.regulator: North Dakota Public Service Commission (ND PSC)
tariffs.summary: A rate available only to data-center-type facilities housing high-density computer-processing technology, with a high minimum load factor and an up-front contribution toward the facilities built to serve them.

customer_type.detail: Available only for data-center-type facilities housing high-density computer-processing technology.

contracted_capacity.detail: Requires a contribution in aid of construction, in advance of building facilities, to recover the utility's estimated installation/removal cost.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — MDU High Density Contracted Demand Response (ND PSC PU-22-337)

tariffs.tariff_name: Large Power Contract Service Tariff
tariffs.summary: A contract-service tariff under which Black Hills will not build new generation for the customer — the customer instead pays for excess capacity above 35 MW purchased from the market — backed by credit support and utility access to the customer's back-up generation.

credit_collateral.detail: Customer may be required to post a deposit or credit support (performance guarantee or letter of credit) held as security for payment.

contracted_capacity.detail: Utility will not build new generation; the customer pays for excess capacity needs beyond 35 MW, which Black Hills purchases from the market.

btm_backup.detail: Customer must agree to allow Black Hills access to its back-up generation.

clean_energy.detail: Black Hills may procure competitively priced renewable resources for the customer.

specific_generation.detail: Utility may procure resources on the customer's behalf.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — Black Hills Large Power Contract Service (WY PSC 20003-146-ET-15)

tariffs.tariff_name: Large Nonresidential Green Energy Affinity Rider (Voluntary Renewable Energy Tariff)
tariffs.summary: A voluntary green tariff giving large nonresidential customers a subscription share of a new renewable facility, or access to clean energy through customer- or utility-signed power-purchase agreements.

clean_energy.detail: Customers subscribe to a share of a new renewable facility or access clean energy via PPAs.

specific_generation.detail: Subscription tied to a specific new renewable facility.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — PGE Green Energy Affinity Rider (OPUC UM 1953)

tariffs.tariff_name: Large Power Rate Schedule
tariffs.summary: Entergy Mississippi's large-power rate schedule, which sets a 30 MW minimum load requirement for service. Entergy maintains data centers pay their full cost of service — a claim contested by ratepayer advocates (see the Ratepayer Protection view).

additional_terms.detail: A May 2026 Synapse Energy Economics report estimated ~$38M in data-center-related costs already charged to Entergy Mississippi residential ratepayers; Entergy disputes the finding.

tariffs.source_title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025) — Entergy Mississippi Large Power Rate (MS PSC 2014-UN-132)

tariffs.tariff_name: Rules for new large-load customers (>100 MW)
tariffs.status_detail: Georgia PSC approved the rule Jan 21, 2025 (Docket 55378).
tariffs.summary: A PSC rule allowing Georgia Power to apply special terms and conditions to any new customer using more than 100 MW, requiring large-load customers to pay the transmission and distribution costs they drive as construction progresses.

min_load.detail: Applies to new customers with demand greater than 100 MW.

customer_type.detail: Targets large-load customers including data centers.

contracted_capacity.detail: Large-load customers must pay the transmission and distribution costs incurred as their construction progresses.

study_cost_recovery.detail: Cost-causation terms assign grid-upgrade costs to the customers driving them.

marginal_pricing.detail: Special terms are designed to limit cost-shifting onto existing ratepayers.

tariffs.source_title: Georgia PSC — Media advisory: rule allowing new power-usage terms for data centers

resources.title: Georgia PSC — Docket 55378

tariffs.tariff_name: Rate Schedule GS-5 (large-load / data-center rate class)
tariffs.status_detail: SCC approved the new rate class in the 2025 biennial review (Nov 2025); effective Jan 1, 2027.
tariffs.summary: A new rate class for the largest electricity users (over 25 MW), including data centers, requiring minimum demand commitments, a 14-year contract term and up-front collateral so grid-upgrade costs driven by data centers are not shifted to other customers.

min_load.detail: Applies to customers using more than 25 MW.

customer_type.detail: New rate class scoped to the largest loads, including data centers.

credit_collateral.detail: Customers must make up-front collateral payments to cover data-center-driven grid-upgrade costs.

contracted_capacity.detail: Must pay for ≥85% of contracted distribution and transmission demand and ≥60% of generation demand.

contract_duration.detail: 14-year contract term for customers signing an ESA on or after Jan 1, 2027.

ramp_times.detail: Optional load-ramp period of up to 4 years, with a minimum annual ramp of 20%.

legislation.title: Virginia SCC Data Center Initiatives (2025–2026)
legislation.summary: SCC's program of measures to ensure data centers pay their own costs, the policy backdrop for the GS-5 rate class.

tariffs.source_title: Virginia SCC — Order on Dominion's 2025 biennial review (new data-center rate class)

resources.title: Virginia SCC — Data Center Initiatives fact sheet

tariffs.tariff_name: Large-load interconnection standards (SB 6 implementation)
tariffs.status_detail: SB 6 signed June 20, 2025; PUCT rulemaking on interconnection standards underway 2025–2026.
tariffs.regulator: Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) / ERCOT
tariffs.summary: Texas Senate Bill 6 directs the PUCT to create interconnection standards for new loads of 75 MW or greater, imposing interconnection fees, financial security, full cost responsibility and emergency curtailment obligations on data centers and other large loads.

min_load.detail: Interconnection standards apply to new loads of 75 MW or greater.

study_cost_recovery.detail: Customers pay 100% of direct interconnection costs, including radial lines and substations.

credit_collateral.detail: Non-refundable $50,000/MW interconnection fee plus financial security of $50,000/MW of requested load.

btm_backup.detail: Large loads must install equipment enabling curtailment during grid emergencies before interconnection.

contracted_capacity.detail: Disclosure of contracted peak demand and behind-the-meter generation required.

additional_terms.detail: Utilities must develop protocols allowing large loads interconnected after Dec 31, 2025 to be curtailed during emergencies.
Expands PUCT/ERCOT oversight of behind-the-meter and co-located generation arrangements.

legislation.title: Texas Senate Bill 6 (2025)
legislation.summary: Overhauls large-load interconnection, transmission cost allocation and co-location rules in ERCOT.

tariffs.source_title: Texas Legislature — Senate Bill 6 (89R) enrolled text

tariffs.tariff_name: Very Large Customer (VLC) tariff
tariffs.status_detail: Wisconsin PSC approved, with modifications, April 24, 2026.
tariffs.summary: A special rate plan for data-center-scale customers in We Energies' territory; the PSC lowered the eligibility threshold from 500 MW to 100 MW and extended the minimum term to 15 years to prevent cost-shifting to existing customers (relevant to Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus).

min_load.detail: Eligibility threshold lowered by the PSC from 500 MW to 100 MW.

customer_type.detail: Scoped to very large / data-center-scale customers.

contract_duration.detail: Minimum initial term extended by the PSC to 15 years to prevent cost-shifting.

contracted_capacity.detail: Minimum-take provisions require the customer to cover its committed demand.

marginal_pricing.detail: PSC modifications target protection of existing ratepayers from data-center cost-shifting.

tariffs.source_title: Wisconsin PSC — Press release on We Energies Very Large Customer tariff decision

tariffs.tariff_name: Amended Interconnection Service Agreement — Susquehanna co-location
tariffs.status_detail: FERC rejected the amended ISA 2–1 on Nov 1, 2024 (189 FERC ¶ 61,078).
tariffs.summary: A federal (not state) co-location case included as the LBL brief's reference point (FERC AD24-11-000): PJM/PPL/Talen sought to raise the co-located load for an Amazon data center at the Susquehanna nuclear plant from 300 MW to 480 MW. FERC rejected the amended ISA, finding PJM had not met its burden to justify the non-standard arrangement.

contracted_capacity.detail: Proposed to increase the co-located data-center load from 300 MW to 480 MW behind the plant's interconnection.

specific_generation.detail: Load co-located directly behind the Susquehanna nuclear units under a bilateral supply arrangement.

btm_backup.detail: Co-located / partially islanded configuration raised cost-allocation and grid-service questions FERC found unresolved.

additional_terms.detail: FERC majority held PJM failed to show its standard ISA was inadequate; the dissent called it a 'first-of-its-kind' configuration needing bespoke review.
Spurred FERC's broader inquiry into large loads co-located at generating facilities (Docket AD24-11-000).

tariffs.utility: Pennsylvania electric distribution companies (statewide model framework)
tariffs.tariff_name: Large Load Model Tariff Framework
tariffs.status_detail: Final order entered May 13, 2026 (adopted 5-0 on April 30, 2026). A model framework Pennsylvania EDCs may incorporate into utility-specific tariff filings, subject to Commission review.
tariffs.summary: First-of-its-kind statewide model tariff framework giving Pennsylvania's electric distribution companies consistent guidance for serving large loads — customers above 50 MW individually or 100 MW in aggregate — with cost-causation, financial-assurance, and interconnection-study standards to protect existing ratepayers from stranded costs.

min_load.detail: Applies to large load customers exceeding 50 MW individually or 100 MW in aggregate.

customer_type.detail: Scoped to large load customers, including data centers, across all PA electric distribution companies.

study_cost_recovery.detail: Utilities must complete interconnection studies within six months; customers bear cost-causation responsibility for studies and upgrades.

credit_collateral.detail: Requires deposits, collateral, and other financial assurances sufficient to mitigate stranded-cost risk from delayed or abandoned projects.

contracted_capacity.detail: Reinforces cost causation: customers driving new infrastructure are responsible for the associated costs to limit cross-subsidization.

contract_duration.detail: Provides guidance on minimum contract terms to back long-lived utility investment; specific term length is set in utility-specific filings.

ramp_times.detail: Provides guidance on load-ramping schedules as part of the large-load contract terms.

exit_fee.detail: Provides guidance on customer exit provisions tied to unrecovered utility investment.

marginal_pricing.detail: Incorporates enhanced guidance on Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) and cost allocation to limit cross-subsidization.

additional_terms.detail: Utilities must complete large-load interconnection studies within six months to improve development predictability.
Large load customers may self-construct certain infrastructure upgrades, subject to utility, safety, reliability, and regulatory standards.
Utilities must maintain public-facing information on large-load interconnection requests and study status.

tariffs.source_title: PA PUC — Final Order establishing first-of-its-kind Large Load Model Tariff Framework

tariffs.tariff_name: Schedule 96 — Large Load Direct Access / large energy use facility rate class
tariffs.status_detail: Approved by Oregon PUC Order No. 26-154 on May 7, 2026; revised tariffs filed June 3, schedules effective June 10, 2026.
tariffs.summary: Oregon's first dedicated large-load rate class, requiring PGE data center and other large customers above 20 MW to cover 100% of distribution upgrades and pay minimum demand charges at 90% of contracted capacity, with contract terms that lengthen with project size — implementing 2025's HB 3546 so growth costs don't shift to residential ratepayers.

min_load.detail: Applies to large loads exceeding 20 MW in PGE territory.

customer_type.detail: Creates a dedicated large-load rate class (Schedule 96) for large energy use facilities, including data centers.

contracted_capacity.detail: Minimum generation and transmission demand charges set at 90% of contracted system capacity, even if the customer uses less.

contract_duration.detail: Contract terms escalate with size: 10 years for smaller loads up to 30 years for projects of 220 MW or more.

exit_fee.detail: Early-termination penalties tied to remaining demand obligations and the unspent value of new distribution investment.

marginal_pricing.detail: Large loads cover 100% of the distribution network upgrades needed to serve them, preventing cost-shift to other ratepayers.

clean_energy.detail: Large-load interconnection approvals are tied to clean-energy availability and Oregon emissions targets (Schedule 96 climate-linked review).

econ_dev_payments.detail: Loads over 100 MW pay a 1¢/kWh surcharge directed to offset residential customer costs and low-income energy burden.

additional_terms.detail: Large-load data center rates rise ~29%, while residential rates fall ~1.3% and small-business rates ~3.7%.

legislation.title: Oregon HB 3546 (2025) — large energy use facilities
legislation.status: Enacted as Chapter 323 (2025), emergency clause; sunsets Jan 2, 2035
legislation.summary: Directs the Oregon PUC to create a new service classification for large energy use facilities that allocates serving costs to those facilities and mitigates risk to other customer classes — the basis for PGE's Schedule 96. Widely referred to as the POWER Act.

tariffs.source_title: Utility Dive — Oregon PUC approves PGE's large-load tariff framework for data centers

tariffs.utility: Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy)
tariffs.tariff_name: Large Load Tariff
tariffs.status_detail: Filed with the Colorado PUC on April 2, 2026; pending review.
tariffs.summary: Proposed Xcel/Public Service Company of Colorado tariff requiring customers above 50 MW (and some 20–50 MW) to cover the transmission, substation, interconnection, and new-generation costs needed to serve them, with 15-year-plus contracts and financial security, so existing customers don't subsidize large new loads such as data centers.

min_load.detail: Applies to customers using 50+ MW at peak; new customers between 20 and 50 MW may also be subject.

customer_type.detail: Large-load tariff aimed at high-demand users such as data centers.

marginal_pricing.detail: Large customers pay for the transmission lines, substations, interconnection upgrades, and new electric generation needed to serve them.

contract_duration.detail: Minimum contract term of 15 years or more.

contracted_capacity.detail: Customers owe a minimum monthly payment toward infrastructure costs even if their load ramps up gradually.

credit_collateral.detail: Financial security requirements add protection if a project is delayed, scaled back, or not completed.

exit_fee.detail: If a large customer exits service early, termination charges recover the remaining cost of project-specific upgrades built, avoiding stranded costs.

additional_terms.detail: Large customers must execute Interconnection Agreements and Energy Service Agreements before receiving electric service.
Public Service Company of Colorado projects large-load customers will make up two-thirds of new demand, needing ~950 MW of new generation over five years.

tariffs.source_title: Xcel Energy — Proposal protects customers from higher bills as data center demand grows

resources.title: DOE/Berkeley Lab — Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (Jan 2025)

tariffs.tariff_name: Ratepayer Protection Tariff (large-load cost allocation framework)
tariffs.status_detail: Filed by Microsoft with the PUCN in May 2026 under Docket No. 20-08014; proposed framework pending commission review.
tariffs.summary: A statewide framework Microsoft proposed to Nevada regulators that would have NV Energy track the substations, generation, and transmission dedicated to each large-load customer and split costs into a customer-paid project share and a grid-benefit share — turning Microsoft's 'paying our way' pledge into an enforceable rate mechanism that shields residential and small-business ratepayers.

customer_type.detail: Statewide framework for allocating costs of large-load (high-load-factor) customers such as AI data centers.

marginal_pricing.detail: Splits costs into a Customer Contributed Share (project-specific infrastructure paid by the customer) and a System Benefit Share (grid-wide benefit reviewed for rate base).

study_cost_recovery.detail: NV Energy maintains a customer-specific asset schedule tracking the substations, generation, and transmission serving each large-load customer.

contracted_capacity.detail: Customers either provide upfront contributions or make ongoing facility payments for the dedicated infrastructure.

exit_fee.detail: A final exit charge applies if a customer departs before cost recovery is complete.

btm_backup.detail: A 'Bring Your Own Power' option lets customers source generation from third parties, reducing overbuild risk.

additional_terms.detail: Projects funded fully upfront may receive PUCN approval within 60 days where no system-benefit cost recovery is sought.

tariffs.source_title: Utility Dive — Microsoft seeks Nevada tariff to shield ratepayers from data center costs

tariffs.tariff_name: Large-Load Security Deposit Tariff (Docket P2025-0677)
tariffs.status_detail: Illinois Commerce Commission approved March 20, 2026; effective immediately.
tariffs.summary: ICC approved ComEd's revised tariff requiring security deposits from large-load applicants requesting 50 MW or more: $1M for 50–200 MW, plus $500K per additional 100 MW above that. Deposits apply toward development costs on completed projects and are refunded (minus incurred costs) on cancellations. Simultaneously, ICC opened a separate investigation (staff report due ~late 2026) into additional consumer-protection mechanisms for data-center-driven distribution upgrades. First approved large-load surety tariff in Illinois.

credit_collateral.detail: $1M deposit for 50–200 MW requests; +$500K per additional 100 MW. Refundable on cancellation minus incurred costs.

min_load.detail: Applies to load interconnection requests of 50 MW and above.

tariffs.tariff_name: Large-Load Cost-of-Service Tariff (ACC Rate Case E-01345A-25-0134)
tariffs.status_detail: Filed with Arizona Corporation Commission in 2025; ACC decision expected by end of 2026.

Includes formula rates tying infrastructure costs directly to the large-load customers who cause them. The ACC hosted a large-load / data-center workshop April 20, 2026 to gather stakeholder input; final order expected late 2026.

customer_type.detail: Rate case explicitly targets extra-large energy users including data centers; formula rates link infrastructure costs to the causative customer.

tariffs.tariff_name: Large-Load Customer Class Proposal (NCUC Rate Case E-7, Sub 1300)
tariffs.tariff_type: Large-load rate case — cost-of-service and class design
tariffs.status_detail: Filed November 20, 2025; NCUC evidentiary hearings summer 2026; decision expected late 2026, new rates effective January 1, 2027.
tariffs.summary: Duke Energy's 2025 rate case is the arena for a major fight over large-load tariff design in North Carolina. The NC Attorney General, NCUC Public Staff, and advocacy groups have independently proposed creating a new large-load customer class (50+ MW) with special rules and rates for data centers, ensuring they pay their own cost of service. Duke has approximately 6 GW of data center demand in its queue. A final order is expected late 2026 with new rates effective January 1, 2027.

customer_type.detail: Proposed new 50+ MW customer class embedded in the broader rate case; not yet formally designated but supported by the AG, Public Staff, and intervening parties.

min_load.detail: 50 MW threshold proposed by multiple parties for the new large-load class.
